Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed chromatin accessibility readout
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined pulse of AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine), then wash out and profile ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN for AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and H3K27ac at days to weeks later. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motif sites after Fos/Jun levels return to baseline would indicate a memory-like state.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion of AP-1 during maintenance phase
ideas.description: Use an inducible degron (dTAG/AID) on JUN/FOS or a dominant-negative (A-FOS) after the initiating stimulus has ended. If primed enhancers close and the enhanced secondary response is lost only when AP-1 is removed during the maintenance window, AP-1 is required for maintaining memory, not just establishing it.

ideas.title: Secondary-stimulus response assay (priming test)
ideas.description: Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq, single-cell) of naive versus previously stimulated cells upon restimulation, with and without AP-1 perturbation at the priming stage. Faster or stronger induction of AP-1 target genes in primed cells, dependent on AP-1 binding at those loci, directly tests memory function.

ideas.title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter and lineage tracking across divisions
ideas.description: Image single-cell AP-1 activity (e.g., FOS-GFP knock-in or AP-1 transcriptional reporter) with lineage tracing through cell divisions after a pulse stimulus. Heritable reporter states in daughter cells, and their dependence on feedback loops, would show whether memory is cell-autonomous and mitotically propagated.

ideas.title: Pioneer function and mitotic bookmarking tests
ideas.description: Perform CUT&RUN/ChIP on mitotic-arrested versus interphase cells and use motif-mutant (CRISPR-edited) enhancers or dCas9-based AP-1 site recruitment/blocking to ask whether AP-1 retention at specific sites is necessary and sufficient to reopen chromatin and sustain gene expression after division. Pair with ordering of AP-1 relative to SWI/SNF (BAF) recruitment and histone marks to define the mechanism.
